open_obligations.what_is_open: The joint status of K1 and K2, and hence the sharp asymptotic order of \(A_T(C)\), is not determined by the frozen proof spine. K1 requires a policy-uniform two-class inequality showing that every common pair \((\pi,\widehat\theta)\) incurs a diverging relative risk on at least one of \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta_-}(C)\) and \(\mathcal P_{T,\beta_+}(C)\). K2 requires one explicit design and estimator, independent of the realized \(\beta\), whose risk is at most \(T^{o(1)}R_T(\beta;C)\) simultaneously over the entire decay interval.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available endpoint priors do not furnish the required cross-class tradeoff. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:rough-prior-low-energy-risk}\) yields a rough-class lower bound only when the rough-prior likelihood energy is small, while Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:smooth-block-prior-risk}\) yields a smooth-class lower bound through the number of monochromatic blocks. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint-certificate-gap}\) gives an explicit cadence with zero monochromatic-block certificate but rough-prior energy of order \(Ts_b^2\), so these two conditions are not complementary. Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint-bump-persistence-risk}\) controls the failure probability of observing at least one homogeneous run, but a single such run can eliminate that certificate without forcing a large smooth-class risk; it therefore does not repair the missing policy-uniform dichotomy. On the upper-bound side, the common \(\beta_-\)-tuned selector gives only a polynomial ratio because the only uniform oracle denominator currently proved is of order \(T^{-1/2}\), whereas the beta-aware upper certificate is of order \(T^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\). Thus the declared results supply neither a divergent two-class factor nor a common subpolynomial procedure relative to the unknown exact oracle risks.
open_obligations.attempted: The low-energy/high-smooth-risk split based on Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem:rough-prior-cadence-kl}\), \(\mathrm{lem:rough-prior-low-energy-risk}\), and \(\mathrm{lem:smooth-block-prior-risk}\) fails on the deterministic cadence certified by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint-certificate-gap}\). Replacing the rough prior by the endpoint bump of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint-bump-persistence-risk}\) also fails to create a frequency-sensitive dichotomy, because its lower bound depends only on the event that at least one qualifying run occurs. For K2, tuning the Markov construction at \(\beta_-\) and using nesting of the classes produces the established common-design bound, but its comparison with Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:exact-positive-oracle-risk}\) remains polynomial rather than \(T^{o(1)}\). A resolution therefore needs either a new supported two-endpoint prior whose Bayes risks obey a policy-uniform cadence tradeoff, or a new multiscale assignment-and-estimation construction together with oracle lower bounds strong enough to evaluate its relative risk.
open_obligations.partial_result: The strongest closed finite-horizon conclusion, realigned to the current exact-\(B\) selector, is \[1\le A_T(C)\le\frac{N_T^\star}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{N_T^{\mathrm{fin}}}{D_T^{\mathrm{bin}}}\le\frac{\sqrt2}{B}\left[\sqrt{(8e-4)\left(1+2^{-1/(2\beta_-+1)}\right)}\,B+\frac C{\beta_-}\right]T^{1/(4\beta_-+2)}.\] For \(T\ge2\), \[N_T^\star=\min\left\{B,\min_{1\le b\le T}U_{T,\beta_-}^{\mathrm{cond}}(b)\right\},\] and the \(B\) branch is the fixed-before-assignment persistent homogeneous-path fair-coin procedure. For every fixed array its risk is \((|\mu_0|+|\mu_1|)/2\le B\), and the admissible constant array attains \(B\), so that branch has exact worst-case risk \(B\). Moreover, \(A_1(C)=1\), while the strongest unconditional two-class factor remains \(g_T=1\). The proved low-energy and endpoint-persistence lower bounds remain valid, but they do not imply K1 or K2; bounded adaptation, logarithmic divergence satisfying both K1 and K2, and polynomial regimes remain compatible with the declared results.
